items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: we all started to be changing to Prince Robertson, and we tried to find everything that he ever recorded.

ctx.x: So -- okay, excuse me. But how about Prince Robertson? That's another great --

Oh, Prince Robertson, man! Prince Robertson, now he was running Coleman Hawkins a tight fight, because the cats were debating -- when I first heard of Prince Robertson was McKinney Cottonpickers-- I said, who is th is cat? Because he was sounding as great as Coleman Hawkins to me, almost, because actually Hawk was my inspiration. And Prince Robertson, man, was running Hawk a close second. And he played with the McKinney's Cottonpickers, and this -- was from New Orleans Prince with some darlings -- and played an…

ever met. And I'm sure if he were living today he would still be a threat to all clarinet and tenor players. He had a unique style. I never will forget when Clyde Hart, as I told you before, was copying the records of the Japain music. He copied a solo of Prince Robinson's that Ben Webster had to play, see?
